# Features

<!-- Generated by scripts/features render from features.toml. Edit features.toml, not this file. -->

Every feature of the Homelab app 1.0.0, where it lives, how it is tested, what it needs and where it is documented. The source of truth is [`features.toml`](../features.toml); `scripts/features check` (part of `scripts/lint`) keeps it honest against the code, the tests, [DeviceTest.md](../DeviceTest.md), the docs and [`server/openapi.yaml`](../server/openapi.yaml).

| Features | Shipped | Partial | Planned | Dependencies | Gaps |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 99 | 72 | 25 | 1 | 41 | 4 |

Adding a feature: one `[[feature]]` entry in `features.toml`, then `scripts/features render`. `scripts/features show <id, file, row, suite, feature flag, link>` answers "which feature is this?".

Columns: **Needs** = server features (`features` in `GET /api/v1/info`), **Tests** = Swift Testing suites or tests, **Phone** = rows of DeviceTest.md (bold = release-blocking).

## Gaps

Shipped or partial features that miss tests, a phone row or docs (and don't say why in `not_needed`):

| Feature | Missing |
|---|---|
| [today-folding](#today-folding) | no DeviceTest row |
| [weather-line](#weather-line) | docs only in the changelog |
| [personality](#personality) | no DeviceTest row for the personality itself (DL10 only touches it) |
| [lessons-card](#lessons-card) | docs only in the changelog |

Not verified (the registry says so in `unsure`):

- [last-report](#last-report): No test checks the last_message section itself; FixtureDecoding only decodes it.
- [widget-status](#widget-status): Widget views are not unit-tested (WidgetKit doesn't build on Linux); only the data rules are.
- [background-refresh](#background-refresh): The BGTask itself only runs on a device; no test covers BackgroundRefresh.run (HomelabUI doesn't build on Linux).
- [install-sidestore](#install-sidestore): Installing the IPA was tested on 2026-11-07; adding the source (I1, I2) waits for the first release.
- [bridge-docker](#bridge-docker): That tailscaled in userspace mode would hand tailnet connections to 127.0.0.1 ports (why compose.yaml uses kernel networking) is from Tailscale's netstack behaviour, not tested here.

### today-folding

**Today is short by design (folds, Also panel)** · Today · shipped · since 2026-11-08

Standard fits two screens, Overkill three, Calm one. Urgent rows (deadlines overdue, today or within 48 h, departure disruptions, to-dos past their time, proposals) never fold; longer lists show 3 rows and "Show N more"; deals, recent downloads, grades and departures are one-line summary rows in an "Also" panel that expand in place; the weather card is left to the hero line; Machines are in Lab only. Overkill adds detail per line. Expanding lasts for the session.

### show-rules

**Show rules (kit)** · Today · partial · since 2026-11-07

One optional rule per Today section says when it shows: Always (the default, and what no rule means), When it needs me, At set times (named windows like Evenings or Weekdays, midnight wrap), and At home or Away once presence comes from Home Assistant (unknown or older than 30 min passes). Overkill ignores rules, Calm adds sections set to "When it needs me" while they need you, Standard shows Machines only with a rule. Old settings save back unchanged. Kit only: the editor and "Hidden now" are the feature show-rule-editor.

### show-rule-editor

**Show rules: editor and "Hidden now"** · Today · partial · since 2026-11-07

Settings → Today → Sections shows each section's rule in words under its name ("Always", "Evenings", Machines "Only in Overkill"; "Not on your servers" when no server can fill it), and a tap opens a sheet: Always, When it needs me (with what that means for the section), Mornings, Daytime, Evenings, Weekdays, Weekends, or Custom with two time pickers and day chips. At home and Away only once presence is set up. While a rule hides a section that has something to show, Today ends with one line "Hidden now: Deals (evenings) · Show"; Show brings them back until the app closes. Without rules Today is exactly as before.

### transport-hardening

**Network hardening and tolerant decoding** · Security · shipped · since 2026-11-04

An ephemeral URLSession (no cookies, no cache), no redirects, answers stop at 8 MB (Home Assistant 32 MB); every field is optional, unknown values fall back, bad items are dropped, server numbers are clamped (Int only through Int(clamping:), a lint check).

### source-status

**Source status in /info** · Server · partial · since 2026-11-07

A Homelab Bridge lists its sources in GET /info under an optional `sources`: per source its name, type, state (ok, failing, never), the last run (`checked`), the last good run (`last_ok`), the short error while failing (no URLs, no keys), `insecure: true` when it skips the TLS check and `plain_http: true` when it sends a key over plain http:// to a host that is not loopback, both as warnings. ### bridge-docker

**Homelab Bridge in Docker (image, compose with a Tailscale sidecar)** · Server · partial · since 2026-11-07

`docker compose up` in server/ runs the Homelab Bridge next to a Tailscale sidecar that is its own tailnet machine: the bridge listens on 127.0.0.1 in the namespace it shares only with the sidecar, `tailscale serve` (HTTPS, login header, never Funnel) is the only way in, keys come from env files, both have a healthcheck. ### source-actions

**Bridge source actions (opt-in)** · Server · partial · since 2026-11-07

Off by default and per item (owner decision 6): only containers, VMIDs or pause lengths listed under a source's `actions` get Docker restart (`restart-container`, the host page's Restart), Proxmox start and clean shutdown (`guest-start`, `guest-stop`) or the ad blockers' pause (`dns-pause`, with a Pause or Resume button on the Blocking row), served as run-actions. The app confirms each press; the server takes only an argument from the list (looked up, never parsed, so prefixed host ids with `:` work), no payload, 30 presses an hour, one per item at a time, answers without URLs or keys, and reads the source again after a press that worked. A card item's button from a source stays only when its action and argument are on the list. Without `actions` there is no /actions route.

### homepage-import

**Import from Homepage** · Server · partial · since 2026-11-07

A `homepage` key in the Homelab Bridge's config reads Homepage's services.yaml at start: every service with an http(s) href becomes a launcher entry (name, url, innermost group, an SF Symbol for well-known icon names, description); `uptimekuma`, `gatus`, `proxmox`, `pihole` (v6 only; a v5 widget is logged as not supported), `adguard`, `sonarr`, `radarr`, `qbittorrent` and `minecraft` (a `gameserver` source) widgets become sources of those types, never with actions (more keys per source, a pause too, by hand with `extra`); other widgets are logged as not yet supported. Keys are taken only as the names of their HOMEPAGE_VAR_/HOMEPAGE_FILE_ placeholders; a key written in services.yaml for an imported widget stops the start with a message that never prints it. Needs PyYAML (in the Docker image); without it the start says so.

- **Swift 6.4 toolchain** (`swift`): Builds the package; Swift 6 strict concurrency, Swift Testing. Linux builds only HomelabKit (KIT_ONLY=1). Unsure: scripts/test-linux uses the tag swift:6.4-noble without the digest that CI pins, so local runs can drift from CI. <https://www.swift.org/install/linux/>
- **iOS 18 or newer** (`ios-18`): Minimum OS of app, widget and extension. The noSwiftUICore linker flag keeps iOS 18 working with the iOS 26/27 SDK.
- **iOS SDK from Xcode 27.1** (`ios-sdk`): xtool takes the iOS SDK from it (`xtool sdk install`). CI's xcode-27 runner is the closest match. Linux builds record the wrong SDK version (xtool issue #351), harmless outside the App Store.
- **xtool** (`xtool`): Turns the SwiftPM package into an app with a widget and a share extension and signs it with a free Apple ID, without Xcode. Unsure: The AppImage's SHA-256 for Linux is not recorded in the repo (docs/SETUP.md asks you to record it yourself). <https://github.com/xtool-org/xtool>
- **xtool 1.24.0 App Group patch** (`xtool-app-group-patch`): xtool 1.24.0 drops the App Group for a free Apple ID, so widgets and the share extension never see the app's data. Patched local build until a release after 1.24.0. <https://github.com/xtool-org/xtool/pull/284>
- **usbmuxd and libimobiledevice** (`usbmuxd`): xtool talks to the iPhone over USB through usbmuxd (Linux).
- **Free Apple ID** (`free-apple-id`): Signs the app: it stops opening after 7 days, 3 active sideloaded apps, 10 new App IDs a week (Homelab uses 3: app, widget, share extension).
- **SideStore** (`sidestore`): Installs and refreshes the app on the phone without a computer; renames bundle IDs and the App Group. <https://sidestore.io>
- **SideStore anisette server** (`sidestore-anisette`): The fix for sign-in error -80045: a remote anisette server instead of on-device anisette.
- **LocalDevVPN** (`localdevvpn`): SideStore's VPN helper for sign-in and refresh; only one VPN at a time, so a Shortcut swaps it with Tailscale.
- **Tailscale (tailscale serve, MagicDNS, HTTPS certificates)** (`tailscale`): The phone reaches the server through the tailnet; `tailscale serve` adds HTTPS and the Tailscale-User-Login identity header the app relies on for token-less servers (and the widgets' own fetch). <https://tailscale.com>
- **Homelab Companion API v1** (`companion-api-v1`): The contract between app and server (server/openapi.yaml). Additions are compatible; a breaking change is /api/v2 and the app shows an update error.
- **Home Assistant REST API** (`home-assistant-api`): The Home tiles read entities and call services directly on Home Assistant (no Homelab server needed).
- **The owner's homelab agent (agent-chat, private)** (`agent-chat`): The real server behind the app: implements every feature flag (documents, search and deals only when their backends are set up), the cards (today, todos, deadlines, parcels, lessons, weather, departures, lab cards) and the Start actions. Lives in a private repo; this repo only has the contract and the reference server.
- **Paperless (server side)** (`paperless`): Where scans and shared PDFs end up; the server files them (OCR) in the background and reports to the chat.
- **Seerr (server side)** (`seerr`): Answers the owner's server's /search and posters, and runs the Request action. Unsure: Only the owner's server uses it; another server can answer /search from anything.
- **willhaben (server side)** (`willhaben`): The used market the server watches for deals; a shared willhaben ad link starts a price check.
- **ntfy push (server side)** (`ntfy`): The server's push for a strong deal opens `homelab://deals`; the app itself has no APNs (free Apple ID).
- **WidgetKit** (`widgetkit`): The widgets (static configuration only; App Intents can't be built with xtool yet).
- **ActivityKit** (`activitykit`): The "Leave by" Live Activity; needs NSSupportsLiveActivities, no entitlement and no extra App ID.
- **VisionKit document camera** (`visionkit`): The Scan screen; importing it autolinks SwiftUICore, hence the noSwiftUICore flag in Package.swift.
- **BackgroundTasks** (`backgroundtasks`): The background refresh (BGAppRefreshTask).
- **UserNotifications** (`usernotifications`): Local notifications and their Approve / Deny actions.
- **LocalAuthentication (Face ID)** (`localauthentication`): The app lock.
- **Keychain (Security framework)** (`keychain`): Tokens, this device only, after first unlock (so the background refresh can read them).
- **App Group entitlement** (`app-group-entitlement`): Shares the server list, settings, the widget snapshot, the outbox and the quick-action counts between app, widget and share extension.
- **Widget extension target** (`widget-extension-target`): Hosts every widget and the Live Activity (one App ID); `-u _main` keeps it from being dead-stripped.
- **Share extension target** (`share-extension-target`): The share sheet entry (one App ID); its principal class is kept from dead-stripping by a linker flag.
- **homelab:// URL scheme and the scan quick action** (`url-scheme`): Links from widgets, pushes, Shortcuts and the static Scan quick action.
- **Python 3** (`python3`): The reference server, its tests, check-live-api, make-source and this registry.
- **Docker** (`docker`): scripts/test-linux runs the Swift tests in the CI image; the patched xtool is built in Docker; scripts/build-bridge-image builds the Homelab Bridge image (buildx for --push).
- **Python 3.14 on Alpine (Homelab Bridge base image)** (`bridge-base-image`): The base of the Homelab Bridge image (server/Dockerfile): small (about 60 MB with the bridge), BusyBox ping works without root. <https://hub.docker.com/_/python>
- **PyYAML (Homelab Bridge image only)** (`pyyaml`): Only in the image (owner, 2026-11-07), for the Homepage import (M1.8). The single-file server stays stdlib-only. <https://pypi.org/project/PyYAML/>
- **tailscale/tailscale container image** (`tailscale-image`): The sidecar in server/compose.yaml: the bridge's tailnet machine, `tailscale serve` from docker/serve.json (TS_SERVE_CONFIG), kernel networking. <https://hub.docker.com/r/tailscale/tailscale>
- **wollomatic socket-proxy** (`docker-socket-proxy`): Optional (compose profile `docker`): only GET /containers/json (a regex per method) for the bridge's Docker source, so the Docker socket never goes into the bridge. Replaced Tecnativa's proxy (2026-11-07), whose CONTAINERS=1 also served /containers/<id>/json (env), logs, archive and export. <https://github.com/wollomatic/socket-proxy>
- **pymobiledevice3** (`pymobiledevice3`): scripts/phone-shots takes screenshots on the iPhone over USB without root.
- **GitHub CLI** (`gh`): Releases: check CI on the commit, create the release with the IPA, its SHA-256 and source.json.
- **actions/checkout** (`gha-checkout`): Checks the repo out in every CI job (persist-credentials off where nothing is pushed).
- **actions/upload-artifact and download-artifact** (`gha-artifacts`): Screenshots and xcodebuild logs as artifacts; the screenshots job publishes them to the ci-screenshots branch.
- **GitHub Pages (classic Jekyll build)** (`github-pages`): Builds and hosts the docs site from main /docs on every push, without a workflow of ours. GitHub sets the versions; Liquid on every page and kramdown instead of GitHub's renderer are why docs/CI.md#docs-site has two rules. <https://pages.github.com/versions/>
- **GitHub-hosted runners** (`gha-runners`): Free standard runners only (public repo); both macOS runners are required.
